extracted.intended_audience: IP statisticians, WIPO users, policymakers, researchers and IP office staff using/producing trademark statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Methodological notes, definitions and figure-specific selection rules used in WIPO's trademark statistical tables and charts (WIPI 2024). Covers how counts are constructed, sample coverage, and selection criteria for displayed origins/offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Paris route and Madrid designations in totals
rubrics_metrics.description: World/figure totals include the number of applications filed directly with national or regional offices (the Paris route), as well as the number of designations received by offices via the Madrid System (where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This wording appears repeatedly (e.g., B1, B2, B4, B5, B35). Users should interpret application and registration totals as combining direct filings and Madrid designations; see glossary for the definition of class count.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and use of class counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures present 'application class count' or 'registration class count' (class counts are the number of Nice classes specified in applications/registrations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See glossary for formal definition of class count. Notes emphasize that figures can report class counts (not just application or registration counts) and that class counts include classes from Paris-route filings and Madrid designations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident versus non-resident assignment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The origin of a trademark application is determined by the residence of the applicant; an application filed at a regional office is considered a resident filing if the applicant is a resident of one of the relevant member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures distinguish resident and non-resident filing activity based on applicant residence. Several charts (e.g., B3, B11, B17) rely on this rule when splitting resident vs non-resident counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute counts versus equivalent counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Some figures distinguish between absolute and equivalent counts for filings abroad; resident applications are excluded when showing abroad activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: B19 shows both absolute and equivalent counts and reports an 'Equivalent/absolute count ratio'. When interpreting abroad filing activity, check whether the figure uses absolute counts (simple class totals) or equivalent counts (adjusted to account for multiple designations).

rubrics_metrics.name: No adjustment for single-class vs multi-class filing systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Data are based on the numbers of applications filed; differences between single-class and multi-class filing systems across IP offices are not taken into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This methodological caveat (explicit in B8 and elsewhere) warns users that comparability across offices may be affected by differing national filing practices (single- vs multi-class).

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure/sample coverage (number of offices)
rubrics_metrics.description: World totals and region totals are WIPO estimates using data covering a specified number of IP offices (e.g., 170 IP offices for many application figures; 155 offices for registrations in force).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific figures note the number of offices underlying totals (e.g., B1/B2: 170 offices; B34: 155 offices). Regional totals specify the number of offices per region (Africa 36, Asia 46, Europe 42, Latin America and the Caribbean 36, Northern America 2, Oceania 8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for origins in GDP-based figure (B30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected 20 origins for 2023 were included if they had a GDP greater than USD 250 billion (PPP) and a resident trademark application class count of at least 20,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: B30 is not an overall ranking but a selection across regions and income groups using the stated GDP and class-count thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for origins in population-based figure (B31)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected 20 origins for 2023 were included if they had a population greater than 2.8 million and a resident trademark application class count of at least 2,600.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: B31 is a selected sample (not exhaustive); users should not interpret it as a universal ranking of all origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrations-in-force metric definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark registrations in force figures refer to the number of trademark registrations currently active, not the number of classes specified in those registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes (B34–B35) explain that registrations in force reflect active trademark rights (which can be maintained indefinitely by renewal fees) and provide insight into the historical trademark life cycle. Interpretations should not conflate registrations count with class count.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variation in registration counts due to examination resources
rubrics_metrics.description: On the basis of an examination, a registration may be issued for a trademark application. The number of registrations issued may fluctuate greatly from one year to the next, in part reflecting the amount of resources that IP offices dedicate to examining trademark applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing registration volumes across offices or years, consider that administrative capacity and resource allocation can materially affect observed registration counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nice Classification goods vs services split
rubrics_metrics.description: In the 45-class Nice Classification, the first 34 classes indicate goods and the remaining 11 refer to services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures that show goods vs services shares (e.g., B24, B27, B29) use this division. See the Nice classification reference for full class descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry sector grouping based on Edital/class groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry sectors used in charts are based on class groups defined by Edital; annex B contains full definitions and composition of Nice goods and services classes for each sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charts showing 'industry sector' shares (e.g., B25–B28) rely on the Edital mapping from Nice classes to sector categories; users should consult annex B for the exact class-to-sector mapping and abbreviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sample selection for top offices and origins
rubrics_metrics.description: Many charts present 'top' offices or origins selected based on 2023 totals (e.g., top 5/top 20 offices or origins).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes explicitly state that selections (top offices/origins) were chosen based on 2023 application or registration totals; results are therefore conditioned on that selection rule and not exhaustive across all offices/origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source and reference date for statistics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each figure includes this source line; users should cite the WIPO Statistics Database and the month/year when referencing these charts or extracting the underlying data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures may use absolute rather than equivalent application class counts for office/origin cross-tables
rubrics_metrics.description: Office and origin data shown in certain tables/figures consist of absolute rather than equivalent application class counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes (e.g., B9, B20, B22) caution readers that displayed tables use absolute (unadjusted) class counts. This affects interpretation when comparing flows between origins and offices and when multi-destination filings occur.
